mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST by more than 3% over one quarter indicates supply chain inflation with weakening housing demand, which compresses corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.03 and HOUST < -0.03 over one quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS from above 4% to below 2% within three months signals an abrupt policy easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls from >4% to <2% within 3 months
regime_hint: policy pivot from tightening to easing
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS above 0.5% month-over-month and a fall in UNRATE below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals labor market softening after expansion, which reduces wage growth pressure and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in GDPC1 above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive quarters signals a robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month moving average +3% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at the 5% level.
